prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Help! Whats wrong with my plant? Had done great for years, now this.

It’s been very low maintenance for years. I water it once a week. Changes made: 1. a couple months ago I moved it further away from the window. (I’ve now moved it back to the window.) 2. about a year ago, I removed the tray that was under it. 3. About 4 months ago, I added soil. I just dug into the soil to see if it felt moist, and found what looked like mold.

Yes, it is.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
This looks like an **Alocasia** or **Colocasia** (elephant ear). The most likely cause is **overwatering with poor drainage, leading to root and stem rot**, made worse by lower light.

## Why I think it's rot
- **Collapsing petioles.** The stems are flopping and drooping instead of holding the leaves up. That happens when the stem bases are mushy and can't support the weight.
- **Yellowing leaves** with a blotchy yellow-green pattern, especially the one on the floor.
- **Crispy brown dead leaves** at the base.
- **Mold in the soil**, which means the soil stays wet too long.
- **Your changes stacked up.** Less light means the plant uses less water, but you kept watering weekly. Added soil may have buried the stems or compacted the top layer so it holds more moisture. The pot also looks like a decorative metal container, and I don't see a drainage hole. Water pooling at the bottom is a common cause of this.

## What to do now
1. **Take it out of the pot** and inspect the roots and tubers or corms.
   - Healthy roots are firm and white or tan.
   - Rotted ones are brown or black, mushy, and smell sour.
2. **Cut away all rotted material** with clean scissors. Remove any stems that are mushy at the base.
3. **Let the plant dry out** for a few hours. If the corm is firm, you can dust cuts with cinnamon or a fungicide.
4. **Repot in fresh, chunky, well-draining mix.** Use potting soil with perlite or orchid bark, roughly 2 parts soil to 1 part perlite. Throw out the moldy soil.
5. **Use a pot with drainage holes.** If you like the metal pot, keep the plant in a plastic nursery pot inside it, and empty any water that collects.
6. **Keep the corm's top at or just above the soil line.** Don't bury the stems.
7. **Cut off dead and collapsed leaves.** Leave the healthy upright ones.

## Going forward
- **Don't water on a fixed schedule.** Water when the top 1–2 inches of soil are dry. With reduced light or in winter, that may be every 10–14 days.
- Give it **bright, indirect light**. Moving it back to the window was a good call.
- Scrape off surface mold, and a bit more airflow will help prevent it from returning.

## Expectations
If the corms are still firm, it will likely recover, though it may lose some leaves and look rough for a while. If the whole base is mush, try to save any firm corm pieces and start them in moist perlite or sphagnum moss. Even a big plant like this can regrow from a healthy piece.

If you tell me what you find when you take it out of the pot, I can help with next steps.
